records.steps: Score and weighted-value products scale as L²d, whereas Q/K/V/output projections scale as Ld². FFN scales linearly in L: C true, D false. A is false for the quadratic products; B is true only if self-attention FLOPs means those products alone.

records.steps: QKᵀ costs O(T²d) and AV costs O(T²d), so both B and C qualify. A row-wise softmax is O(T²), not O(T²d); D is O(Td).

records.answer: D: scaling limits softmax saturation and vanishing gradients.
records.steps: Independent unit-variance components yield dot-product variance proportional to d_k; dividing by √d_k controls scale. A is not the main motivation; B does not reduce asymptotic cost; C is guaranteed by softmax.
A: heads can learn different relations. C: standard equal head width is d_model/h. B: more heads do not generally reduce memory and score matrices grow with head count. D: heads may overlap.
Each head produces a `[12, 12]` score matrix per sequence, hence 4×2×12² = 1152.
Float32 uses 4 bytes; 8×1000²×4/10⁶ = 32 MB and 16×1000²×4/10⁶ = 64 MB. The increase is (64−32)/32×100%.
One head has W_Q shape `[512, 64]`, so 512×64 = 32768 matrix entries; bias is not part of the matrix.

The dot-product variance grows with d_k, and √d_k scaling prevents excessively saturated softmax and tiny gradients. A: scalar scaling changes no shape; B: adds/removes no learned parameters; D: does not normalize vector lengths.
Every standard encoder layer preserves sequence length and model width. A pools tokens, B treats layers as tokens, and D concatenates layer outputs, none of which is specified.

A and D follow from separate learned head projections and attention patterns. B is a useful mathematical analogy: parallel learned transformations extract different features, although heads are dynamic attention operators rather than convolution kernels. C is false: standard fixed total width gives the same projection parameter count as one head.

The original encoder has unmasked multi-head self-attention and position-wise FFNs. C belongs to decoder cross-attention, and D describes the causal masked decoder self-attention, not the standard encoder.

records.steps: In an original Transformer encoder, each unpadded position can attend bidirectionally, while causal masking is used in the decoder. Thus assertion true, reason false; A and B require true reason, and D and E falsely reject the assertion.
For Q, K and V, 3×4×256×64 = 196608 entries; W_O has 256×256 = 65536. Total 262144; biases excluded.
Original T5 uses two FFN matrices `[768,3072]` and `[3072,768]`: 2×768×3072=4718592, ignoring bias.
The encoder output is `[5,20,64]`, preserving batch, padded sequence length and hidden width: 5×20×64=6400.

In Bahdanau attention the decoder state scores encoder states and the context is their weighted sum. B is false because weights run over encoder states, not all decoder states; D is false because those states are retrieved throughout decoding.
The original PNG uses QᵀK, consistent with tokens as columns of X; Q=K=X because W_Q=W_K=I. Thus QᵀK=[[1,0,1],[0,1,1],[1,1,2]] and its trace is 1+1+2=4. The transcription incorrectly writes QKᵀ.

The source image specifies column-token QᵀK=[[1,0,1],[0,1,1],[1,1,2]]. The indicated pairs have scores A=0; B=C=D=E=1. Scaling by √2 does not change the ranking, and within the learn query A also has the smallest row-softmax weight.
Every head computes 6²=36 scores per sequence; four additional heads therefore add (8−4)×36=144.
The last encoder output retains shape `[8,32,128]`, independent of the number of layers and heads; 8×32×128=32768.
